narrative.overview:
The interface is the self-serve mala stall itself. A chili-red signboard hangs overhead, and a laminated price board ruled in ink doubles as the tier picker. Below them sits a real 3D counter: brushed steel bins of low-poly ingredients, a pair of red-gripped tongs, and a red perforated plastic basket on a steel scale with a green LCD. Checking out prints a thermal receipt. Every surface stands in for a physical object at the counter. The running weight and price stay the loudest thing in the DOM, because learning them is the point.

The DOM chrome is compact and phone-first: a single column (480px, widening to 760px on large screens), full device height, one hand. Archivo Variable carries every interface role with tabular numerals. The only other type is system monospace, and only on machine-made surfaces: the scale LCD and the receipt. Depth comes from the 3D scene's light and contact shadows. The DOM stays mostly flat, apart from the tags and the printer that sit on top of the scene.
keyCharacteristics: Chili-red signboard header holding mode pills and the live grams / S$ readout.
Ink-ruled white price strip whose cells are the tier tabs, each keyed by a tier swatch.
A 3D steel counter: bins with white DOM price tags, tongs that follow the pointer, a perforated red basket on a scale with a green LCD.
Low-poly, flat-shaded ingredients drawn at 1.3x, falling onto the pile under gravity with no bounce.
A chili action bar with the piece count, an Empty basket link and a cream checkout button.
A dark receipt printer that feeds monospace paper with a torn zigzag edge and a rubber stamp.

rules.name: The Amber Is Money Rule
rules.body: Amber marks prices, budgets and limits, plus the printer's working LED. It is never a general highlight.

rules.name: The Swatch-Only Tier Rule
rules.body: Tier colours appear only as small swatches next to a tier's name. They never fill cells or text. The 3D ingredients carry their own food colours instead.

rules.name: The Machine Palette Rule
rules.body: LCD green and receipt paper belong to the stall's machines (scale and printer). They never become UI surfaces.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals are on for the whole app, so climbing totals never shift sideways.

rules.name: The Machine Type Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only where a machine prints it: the scale LCD and the receipt. Everything a person reads as UI is Archivo.

rules.name: The Scene Owns Depth Rule
rules.body: Physical depth lives in the 3D scene's light and contact shadows. DOM shadows stay small and are used only on objects laid over the scene (tags, LCD, printer, entry card).

dos: Do keep tabular numerals on every number, and units in a `small` at 0.35 to 0.4em.
Do use pills for chrome toggles and buttons, square ruled cells for the price strip, and 2 to 16px radii for printed or mounted objects.
Do set pressed and selected states as an ink/cream swap: cream on chili-deep, ink on cream.
Do start press feedback at `scale(0.96)` over 100ms with `--ease-smooth-out` on everything you press, and take state colour changes at 150ms.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px tall for controls (56px for strip cells).
Do pin DOM labels (tags, LCD) to their 3D anchors every frame, rather than drawing text into the scene.
Do keep 3D motion damped and physical: gravity onto the pile, springs back to the bin, no bounce.
Do keep an accessible non-3D path for adding and removing pieces.
donts: Don't use amber for anything other than money, limits and the printer's working LED.
Don't fill surfaces or text with tier colours. They are swatches only.
Don't use monospace outside the scale LCD and the receipt.
Don't use LCD green or receipt paper as UI surfaces.
Don't add heavy DOM shadows. Depth belongs to the 3D scene.
